steps.thought: I will list all available tests on the station to understand what diagnostic tools and procedures we can use to check the drone subsystems.

tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: Run power_on_selftest to quickly check all digital buses (I2C, UART, CAN) and boot status with minimal cost.
steps.observation: Power-on selftest failed with a camera sensor ID read error, while all I2C, UART, and CAN bus enumerations succeeded. This points directly to a camera ribbon or sensor fault.

hypotheses.rationale: Camera sensor ID read failed during power-on selftest, which is commonly caused by a loose or damaged CSI ribbon cable.
Failure to read camera sensor ID during boot can also indicate a dead or unpowered camera sensor module.

steps.thought: I will run the camera_selftest to gather more specific error data on the camera sensor, distinguishing between a ribbon fault and a dead sensor.
steps.observation: The camera selftest confirms that the sensor ID is not readable, the self-test fails, and the frame rate is 0 fps with no CSI CRC errors, ruling out data corruption and pointing firmly toward either a damaged or loose CSI ribbon cable or a dead camera sensor.

hypotheses.rationale: Failure to communicate with the camera sensor ID and complete lack of frames strongly implicate a loose or damaged CSI ribbon cable preventing power or communication.
Complete unresponsiveness of the camera sensor during both boot and self-test can also be caused by an internal hardware failure on the sensor module itself.

steps.thought: Search the failure library to see how previous technicians differentiated between camera ribbon cable faults and dead camera sensors.

args.query: camera sensor ID read failed frame rate 0

matches.title: Camera self-test fails with CSI CRC errors
matches.symptom_summary: Camera sensor ID reads correctly but self test fails. Frame rate below 28 fps and many CSI CRC errors on the data lanes.
matches.root_cause: CSI ribbon cable creased or partially inserted in the connector.
matches.rework_notes: Reseat the ribbon; replace it if creased.

matches.title: Camera frame rate low, no CRC errors
matches.symptom_summary: Camera self test reports frame rate around 15 fps with zero CRC errors and sensor ID OK. Camera firmware version string does not match the release.
matches.root_cause: Camera module shipped with old firmware set to a low frame rate mode.
matches.rework_notes: Update camera firmware. Zero CRC errors separates it from a ribbon fault.

matches.title: Camera not detected, no frames
matches.symptom_summary: Power-on self test cannot read the camera sensor ID. Camera self test fails with zero fps and zero CRC errors, meaning no data arrives at all.
matches.root_cause: Dead image sensor on the camera module.

steps.observation: The failure library search shows that FL-012 matches the exact symptom profile of unreadable sensor ID, zero frame rate, and zero CRC errors (indicating complete lack of communication due to a dead sensor), while FL-011 involves CRC errors. Both CAMERA_RIBBON_FAULT and CAMERA_SENSOR_DEAD remain viable, but the failure library gives slightly more historical weight to a ribbon or sensor hardware fault.

hypotheses.rationale: Complete lack of sensor communication and zero frames with zero CRC errors closely aligns with a loose or damaged CSI ribbon cable preventing interface power or signaling.
Historical records indicate that total camera unresponsiveness at boot and selftest can stem from an internal dead image sensor on the module.

steps.thought: I will propose replacing the camera module as the failure library points strongly to CAMERA_SENSOR_DEAD given the complete lack of sensor ID and zero frame rate, though a ribbon fault is also possible. I have sufficient confidence to perform the rework.
steps.observation: Rework applied; full suite passed: True.
